name: Sylvie Goddard
bio: Wife of James Goddard ('Kit'), and a member of George Ives's household: Cook records that on marrying, Goddard brought her into the house too, and that their daughters were known there as 'the 2 Kit girls'. Her presence makes the household's composition plain - a married couple and their children living inside the domestic circle Ives called 'my little circle in the world'.
bio_note: From Cook 2014 printed p. 96 (repo PDF 107, folio confirmed), read as a page image 2026-08-03. Cook gives her only as 'his wife Sylvie' - maiden name, dates and marriage date are not stated in the page read. Cook's printed p. 100 reportedly adds that she kept house for Ives and that she and James remained until their deaths, with the daughters staying until the early 1940s (one, Therese, still visiting in 1944); that page is known so far only from the PDF text layer and is flagged as a pointer on the marriage record pending verification at the rendered page. DATES: NOT FOUND; RECORDED AS UNRECOVERED (2026-08-03). She is the least documented member of the household in Cook, who says so himself: her domestic labour 'also went largely without comment' (printed p. 102). He gives her no maiden name, no marriage date and no dates of life; the only chronological facts are that she came into the house on marriage, that she predeceased Ives (her legacy is described as reapportioned 'after Sylvie's death'), and that her daughters stayed until the early 1940s. Searched so far, WITHOUT RESULT: Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), repo PDF - every occurrence of the surname in the whole book, plus the endnotes and bibliography for the household chapter; the Ives repo transcripts (ives_diaries_burnet.txt, ives_letters_burnet_collated.txt, ives_letters_burnet_transcription.txt, ives_lewis_correspondence_2026-06.md), which contain no occurrence of any of the household surnames; and the open web, which returned only the Palgrave chapter version of Cook's same text ('George Ives, Queer Lives and the Family') and no dates. Cook is the only scholar to have written this household up and he dates their arrivals, their departures and Ives's will, but never a person: he gives no birth or death date for any member of the household. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: census, GRO index and probate research on common English surnames - work so far could not do. Ives's own proved will (Cook, printed pp. 109-110), which leaves the Adelaide Road house to Bloodworth and Saunders, names Bloodworth an executor and portions the Goddards, is the natural documentary starting point, since a grant of probate fixes addresses and often identifies legatees.
